title: State, identity and shared access
description: Keep totals and counts in closures, change one link and watch every alias follow, guard an account with a password, count pairs by identity, then share one balance between several passwords.

learned: Build closures that each keep their own state, and tell commands from ordinary calls.
Change one link in place and predict what every alias sees.
Count objects by identity, remembering each before following its parts.
Share one piece of state between several access routes without copying it.
recap.invariant: Each account retains one balance reached by all its authorized operations and aliases; rejected operations preserve it.
recap.complexity: In a stack of n pairs whose parts both point to the pair below, counting by path meets 2**n-1 pairs while counting by identity meets n. A request through d connected services is passed on d times.
recap.common_mistake: Counting equal contents as one identity, or creating a new balance for a new credential.
in_real_programs: Python nonlocal updates an enclosing binding.
Shallow container copies can retain shared mutable elements.

retrieval.question: Module 2: what survives when a closure creator returns?
retrieval.answer: The environment containing bindings reachable through the returned function.
